The seven unchanged rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: validation in a @doc false function called from a one-line quote is clean under Keep quote blocks small, and a route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote is violated even when validation runs in the macro body outside quote (haiku-1, haiku-2); the use rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc (haiku-2's comes after the example, violated); __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for both in sonnet-2, the run that omits @doc false on both); String.to_atom on route text from the router's source (opus-1 line 174, haiku-1 line 102, haiku-2 line 121, sonnet-1 line 123, sonnet-2 line 117) is not counted under the atom rule; `if not ... raise` validation is not counted under the branching rule.

Do: rule, graded against the current text. Violated by haiku-2 only, line 110 `names = for {:param, name} <- segments, do: name`, decided by "A `for` always takes `do ... end`: its generators and filters already fill the head." Nested calls and tuples on do: are clean under "A `do:` body is one expression on the head's line: a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not." (e.g. opus-1 line 89, haiku-1 line 61, haiku-2 line 41, sonnet-1 line 67, sonnet-2 line 85). No run puts a fn or an argument-carrying capture on a do: (the one-line fns of haiku-1 54, sonnet-1 61-62 and sonnet-2 72 are bindings inside block bodies); no run writes a one-line if ..., do:, else:; every other for is a block (opus-1 153-155 and 168-170, haiku-2 65-67, 106-108 and 136-138). Mixed functions set each block clause apart (opus-1 module_name?/1, haiku-1 bind_segments/3 and validate_path!/2, haiku-2 parse_segment!/2, sonnet-1 find_route/2 and match_segments/3, sonnet-2 match_segments/3). No do: body on a line of its own in any file. Guarded one-expression blocks are not counted (opus-1 93-95 and 143-145, sonnet-1 75-77 and 92-94, sonnet-2 105-107). Two unguarded one-expression blocks would fit on the head's line: sonnet-1 103-105 `def __match__(routes, request_path) do` / `find_route(routes, split(request_path))` / `end` (82 joined) and sonnet-2 113-115 `defp segments(path) do` / `Enum.map(split(path), &segment/1)` / `end` (60 joined); neither the old nor the current text requires do: for a fitting one-expression body, and 2026-10-23 did not count sonnet-2's identical compile_path/1, so neither is counted. Every other unguarded one-expression block joins to more than 98 characters.

One expression per line, and tabular clauses (new; no earlier sweep verdict), graded against the current text; all five clean. Deciding sentence: "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces.", with "Count expressions, not calls or brackets" for nested-call heads and "A `fn` reads the same way: `fn {customer_id, count} -> {-count, customer_id} end` holds a pattern and one expression and stays on one line" for the one-line fns (haiku-1 54, sonnet-1 61-62, sonnet-2 72). Sequences and nested constructs sit below their heads in every run. Compact case clauses appear only in haiku-1 79-80 (`{:ok, params} -> {:ok, handler, params}` / `:error -> nil`), one pattern and one expression each, a mapping with one fallback row; sonnet-1 131-137 and sonnet-2 95-101 break theirs. haiku-2's one-line for at line 110 sits inside a block body, not on a head's line, and is graded under the do: rule's for sentence, as in 2026-10-31-check-2.

Pipeline rule, graded against the current text (its row now names macro-dsl; 2026-10-23 listed one-line pipelines under other_violations). Deciding sentence: "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short". All five clean: haiku-1 (96-99), sonnet-1 (56-59, 107-111) and sonnet-2 (67-70) put each |> on its own line under the value; opus-1 line 83 and haiku-2 line 62 write the two __before_compile__ steps as the nested call `Enum.reverse(Module.get_attribute(env.module, :tiny_router_routes))`, which "or become a nested call when there are only two" allows, so they are clean rather than not exercised (as 2026-10-31-check graded sonnet-1). The one-line __before_compile__ pipeline that every Haiku run wrote in 2026-10-23 and both 2026-10-31-check batches is gone.

The renamed `->` rule (Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line) is outside this case's list: haiku-1 79-80's compact clauses each hold one expression read at a glance, and the broken cases in sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 hold a clause that continues the recursion or a nested fn body; nothing to list. Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call is listed for opus-1 (two raise calls whose message argument is a string concatenation spread over two lines), to the standard of 2026-10-31-check-2 haiku-1; haiku-2's compile_error!( caller, "..." ) calls at 93-96 and 123-126 put each argument on one line and are not listed.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run: the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex plus empty MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex (sonnet-2 defines both in its own file, so it got no handlers.ex; a second copy with those two modules moved to handlers.ex gives the same result). opus-1 and sonnet-1 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:match, 1}) report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (runtime). haiku-1 and haiku-2 (Macro.expand(handler, caller)) and sonnet-2 (handler passed unexpanded into the quote that calls __define__/3 in the module body) report alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (compile). All five compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3).

Bad declarations: each project loaded with mix run, then Code.compile_string compiled a router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All ten fail while the router compiles: opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 with ArgumentError from the @doc false __define__/3 that get's quote calls; haiku-1 and haiku-2 with CompileError (nofile:3: route path must be a string..., route handler must be a module name...) raised during macro expansion. Only opus-1 also rejects a lowercase atom such as :foo as a handler; the other four accept it (not a rule).

Format: haiku-1 and haiku-2 pass mix format --check-formatted as delivered (both ran mix format, which put parentheses on the two get calls). opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 fail, matching result.json format_ok false, and in each the only change mix format makes is parentheses on the two bare get calls of the example router; each passes with locals_without_parens: [get: 2]. opus-1 checked in a project with that .formatter.exs, deleted the project, delivered no .formatter.exs and documented the option in @moduledoc lines 37-40; sonnet-1 saw the check fail, fixed its other moved line (a guard it dropped) and left the get calls bare; sonnet-2 saw the check fail and made no change. Per the standard, these are noted in checks, not under Before you finish.
